texts: good. the full name is one symbol with its own Name atom, the kind word inside the name fills one ordinary type atom, and the seven elders ride a counted group. One cross-sentence caution: "The Council of Keepers" and the bare "The Council" of the later sentences yield different symbols, so use the full name wherever you want them to be the same body.

mixed: "new members" is turned into a specific group of members plus a side rule asserting each of them is new, which a habitual clause never claims, and "by consensus" has no proper slot so it lands in the Instrument head meant for a tool or channel. Rewrite as "The Council appoints a new member by consensus." — one indefinite member then carries "new" directly and no specific set is asserted; the method phrase is the only remaining stretch, and no wording of it parses better.

mixed: "for life" has no licensed carrier — the duration head takes a duration adverb such as "briefly", and the parse fills that slot with the noun "life" instead. Rewrite as "A Council member serves permanently." — a duration adverb fits the slot exactly and, for a mortal member, says the same thing.

good. "may" over a kind subject gives the kind-level permission norm on council_member with its genus member, which is precisely the licensed form, at the plain-norm truth value. The open question of whether capitalized "Council" in a premodifier should fuse into the kind or name a separate entity costs nothing here, so leave the sentence as it stands.

bad: "includes" leaves no trace in the parse — the whole clause is rendered as bare membership links — and the compliant repair drops those links in favour of seven opaque "include" events, so on either reading the fact you actually want (these seven make up the Council) is not recorded as membership. Rewrite as "Meren Tallowhand, Old Vesh, Brindle Coombe, Sailsworn, Aelis Brae, Norren, and Wynne Coombe are members of the current Council." — a copular clause with a coordinated subject types each person as a member and links each one to the Council directly, which is the membership record the enumeration is for.

good. the kinship follows the possessive route exactly — Wynne typed as a cousin plus the opaque possession link to Brindle — with both multi-word names as single symbols and no invented typing for Brindle. The relation is stored in one direction only, since the mutual-relation tag is reserved for copular wordings, but nothing this sentence states is lost.
